rubric:
# Same-job pair labels: rubric

A deck tool suggests swapping card OUT for card IN in the same role, claiming IN does "the same job"
(often "for N less mana"). For each pair, judge as an experienced Commander (4-player) player whether
IN really does OUT's job. Read ONLY the oracle text, type line and mana cost given for both cards.
NEVER use memory of what a card does.

Some pairs carry `priorLabel`/`priorWhy` from an earlier reader. Treat it as a hypothesis: agree only
if the text supports it; disagree when it does not, and say so.

Labels:
- `"same"`: a player would swap these without losing the job (same effect on the same things, same
  delivery class; differences only in cost or small upside).
- `"weak"`: same family of effect, but a material difference a player would notice (a cost mode, a
  drawback, a narrower target, something given back).
- `"different"`: not the same job (different effect, different recipient, conditional where the other
  is not, removal vs protection, AND-vs-OR targets, singleton-dead conditions...).

Output one JSON object per pair, input order, exactly these fields:
- `role`, `out`, `in`: names as given.
- `source`: as given (`page` = the site shows it, `player` = a pair a player would call the same).
- `label`: `"same"` | `"weak"` | `"different"`.
- `differs`: array of the parts that differ, from this closed list: `effect` (what it does), `keywords`
  (which keywords granted), `recipient` (who/what it affects: one target vs all yours vs each), `whatItHits`
  (types it can answer, AND vs OR), `control` (whose: any vs opponent's), `duration` (until end of turn vs
  permanent), `delivery` (instant / sorcery / Equipment / Aura / permanent / activated), `amount` (how
  much: fixed vs per-X vs equal-to, -1/-1 vs -X/-X), `conditions` (a condition one has), `givesBack`
  (the opponent gets something), `cost` (mana value, equip cost, alternative cost, life, spree/mode
  cost), `speed` (instant vs sorcery), `role` (OUT is not really in the stated role). Empty if `same`
  with no difference beyond a cheaper mana cost; include `cost` whenever costs differ.
- `priorAgree`: true/false if a prior label was given (map prior "yes"/"plausible" to same, "weak" to
  weak, "no" to different), null otherwise.
- `why`: ONE sentence quoting the decisive words of both texts.

Write the array as JSON to the output file given to you.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Explore's "may play an additional land" is its whole point, while Acumen's "first strike until end of turn" has nothing to do with card draw.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Syphon Mind draws "a card for each card discarded this way" (up to three in a 4-player pod) via forced discard, while Acumen just grants first strike and draws one.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: "Draw a card for each permanent you control of that type" scales with board state; Birthday Escape only ever draws one.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: "Draw cards equal to the greatest power among non-Human creatures" scales with the board, while To Arms! untaps creatures and draws exactly one.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: "Draw cards equal to the greatest power" plus a free spell dwarfs Acumen's first strike plus a single draw.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Sign in Blood draws two for {B}{B}, but Avarice's draw mode needs its base cost plus "+ {B}{B}" to draw three and lose 3 life, a pricier and bigger version of the same job.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Deep Analysis draws two with no life cost up front (only flashback costs "3 life"), while Avarice's draw mode always costs "lose 3 life" and is a sorcery, not an instant held up for flashback value.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: "Discard two cards" permanently loses cards to the graveyard while Brainstorm's "put two cards from your hand on top of your library" keeps them, a real mechanical difference defensible only as "both cantrip for net one card."

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Urban Evolution keeps all three cards and adds "play an additional land", while Amass the Components nets only two cards since one goes "on the bottom of your library" — a real loss of value, not a plain swap.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Winnow only works "if another permanent with the same name is on the battlefield", a condition that is dead in a singleton format where Mortify just destroys target creature or enchantment outright.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Surge only hits a permanent "an opponent controls" (narrower than Beast Within's any permanent) and hands back a revealed card sharing a type instead of a fixed 3/3 token.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Decimate destroys four named targets you pick, while Misguided Rage is "Target player sacrifices a permanent of their choice" — an edict the opponent controls, not targeted removal at all.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Unwanted Remake's destroy is the same but it hands the controller a manifest dread, which "puts one onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2" and can flip into something bigger, unlike Terminate's clean kill.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Trophy is restricted to a permanent "an opponent controls" (Beast Within hits any permanent) and gives back only a searched basic land rather than a 3/3 token — both real, noticeable differences, not a plain same.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Flourish can't hit planeswalkers ("artifact or creature you don't control" only), hands the controller a free spell cast, and "Demonstrate" lets an opponent copy the spell too.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: "Target artifact creature" is an AND requirement (must be both), not an OR, so Molten Frame can't touch Terminate's any-creature target.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Same AND problem: "target artifact creature" excludes the vast majority of creatures Infernal Grasp's "target creature" can hit.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Hex unconditionally destroys six creatures; the Offering is a legendary sorcery ("only if you control a legendary creature or planeswalker") that destroys just "up to one target creature or planeswalker."

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both destroy target creature, deny regeneration, and give the controller "a 3/3 green [token]" — the token's name (Ape vs Frog Lizard) is cosmetic, so the prior "no" is wrong by its own stated reasoning.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Toxic Deluge's "-X/-X" scales with life paid, while Nausea is a flat "-1/-1", a different order of magnitude as a wipe.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both simply "destroy all creatures"; Fumigate's life gain is pure upside and the cost difference (reducing cost vs flat {3}{W}{W}) is only a cost swap, not a changed job.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Boompile only works if you "win the flip" on a coin toss, and hits all nonland permanents rather than the Disk's artifacts/creatures/enchantments only.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Their Name Is Death spares artifact creatures ("nonartifact creatures" only) while Bontu's Last Reckoning hits everything but leaves "lands you control don't untap during your next untap step" as a drawback.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Mutilate scales "-1/-1 ... for each Swamp you control" while Cry is a flat -2/-2 plus a graveyard-exile clause Mutilate never has.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Raise the Palisade bounces ("return ... to their owners' hands") using one chosen type, while Harsh Mercy destroys and lets "each player chooses a creature type", a different effect and a different chooser.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Wash Out bounces "all permanents of the color of your choice" (any permanent type, one color), nothing like Day of Judgment's destroy-all-creatures.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Austere Command's "choose two" can hit creatures AND artifacts/enchantments in one cast, while Cleansing Nova's "choose one" forces picking creatures OR artifacts-and-enchantments, a real loss of flexibility.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Winds of Rath spares creatures "that aren't enchanted", a real condition Day of Judgment's unconditional "destroy all creatures" doesn't have.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Nix only counters a spell "if no mana was spent to cast it", a hard restriction Counterspell's unconditional counter doesn't carry.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Disdainful Stroke needs mana value 4+; Nix needs the spell to be free — unrelated restrictions, not the same filter.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Laquatus's Disdain only counters "a spell cast from a graveyard", a near-dead condition compared to Absorb's unconditional counter.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Both are soft counters, but "pays {1}" is a much lower tax than "pays {2} plus an additional {1} for each Faerie you control."

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Cateran Summons can only find "a Mercenary card", while Diabolic Tutor can find any card in the library.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Trapmaker's Snare is restricted to "a Trap card" and puts it straight into hand, unlike Long-Term Plans' any-card search that goes "third from the top."

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: "Exile the top five cards" plus an extra land drop is much bigger than Rob the Archives' "exile the top two cards" with no land bonus.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both add "one mana of any color" usable by the deck (Signet's colors are always within "your commander's color identity"), differing only in cost and Darksteel Ingot's lost "Indestructible".

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Hexproof and haste for equip {1} is nothing like +3/+3 and selective protection for "Equip commander {3}" / "Equip {5}."

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Shroud at equip {0} versus protection-and-a-pump at triple-to-quintuple the equip cost is a different tool entirely.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Unbreakable Formation's indestructible is unconditional, while Break of Day only grants it under "Fateful hour — If you have 5 or less life."

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Darksteel Mutation neuters the target to a 0/1 with no abilities — that's removal of the creature, not protection like Shardmage's Rescue's hexproof-and-buff.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Indestructible for all your creatures beats protection "from non-Human creatures" only, a narrower and different keyword.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Unblockable-and-shroud for equip {2} is a different tool from +3/+3-and-protection at equip {3}/{5}.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Bathe in Light grants protection to a group sharing a color ("each other creature that shares a color"); Armor of Shadows only pumps and grants indestructible to one creature.

pairs.in: And They Shall Know No Fear
pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Akroma's Will can grant a full keyword package to all your creatures; the other card only buffs creatures "of the chosen type", a narrower recipient with weaker effect.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both grant indestructible to one thing; Blacksmith's Skill is a strict upgrade, hitting "target permanent" and adding hexproof plus a conditional +2/+2.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Hour of Reckoning spares tokens ("all nontoken creatures"), while End Hostilities hits every creature plus "all permanents attached to creatures", a broader and different sweep.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Crush Contraband can "choose one or both" to exile an artifact and an enchantment in one spell, while Fate Forgotten only ever exiles one permanent.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Endless Atlas needs "three or more lands with the same name" to draw at all, while the Top's draw ability sends itself back to the library each time ("put this artifact on top of its owner's library"), a different repeatable-draw problem entirely.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Damning Verdict spares any creature "with no counters on them", a real condition Day of Judgment's unconditional destroy-all lacks.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Ancient Excavation draws up to your whole hand size then discards that many, while Evermind is just "Draw a card" with a splice ability — wildly different amounts and mechanics.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Both draw two cards, but See Beyond nets one fewer because it must "shuffle a card from your hand into your library", and Thoughtcast's affinity can make it much cheaper.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both "draw three cards" for the same mana value; Harmonize simply drops the "lose 3 life" cost Ambition's Cost pays.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: A single Spree mode of Explosive Derailment costs its base plus "+ {2}" (pricier than Abrade's flat {1}{R}) though it deals 4 damage instead of 3.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls "until this enchantment leaves the battlefield" word for word; Conclave Tribunal only adds Convoke as an alternate cost.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Kindred Dominance selectively destroys creatures outside one chosen type; Living Death instead has every player sacrifice their board and reanimate their whole graveyard, a completely different effect.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Windfall discards hands first and draws "equal to the greatest number ... discarded" (scales with hand size), while Burning Inquiry draws a flat three then discards three at random — different order and different amount.

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Mana Geyser scales off "each tapped land your opponents control" while Rite of Flame scales off copies of itself in graveyards — unrelated conditions producing very different amounts.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both "Destroy all creatures"; Wrath of God's extra "They can't be regenerated" clause is vestigial against modern decks.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: "Destroy all creatures. They can't be regenerated." is identical text in both, just a different color.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Both exile target creature, but Swords gives the controller life "equal to its power" while Path lets them ramp with a basic land "onto the battlefield tapped", a materially different giveback.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: The oracle text is identical: "Search your library for up to two basic land cards ... put one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand."

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Arcane Signet always makes your commander's colors, while Fellwar Stone depends on "a land an opponent controls could produce", which can whiff or miss colors you actually need.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Dimir Signet pays {1} to get both colors at once, while the Talisman taps for colorless free or one color for "1 damage to you", a different cost/amount tradeoff for the same color pair.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Sign in Blood can target any player ("Target player draws two cards"), while Night's Whisper is locked to "You draw two cards", a real loss of flexibility.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both destroy target permanent and give a 3/3 token back; only the token's creature type (Elephant vs Beast) differs.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Hexproof still allows the controller to target their own creature while "shroud" on Greaves blocks that too, plus equip {1} versus equip {0}.

pairs.label: same
pairs.why: Both "Counter target spell" for {U}{U}; Mana Drain's bonus mana next main phase is pure upside on an identical core effect.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: "Target nonblack creature" and "target nonartifact creature" exclude different creature pools, so each misses things the other would hit.

pairs.label: weak
pairs.why: Nature's Lore can grab any "Forest card" (including nonbasic Forests) and puts it in untapped, while Rampant Growth is limited to a basic land entering tapped.
